name: a100
description: NVIDIA A100 SXM4 (GA100, Ampere, sm_80) at its 1410 MHz boost clock: one Vortex core per SM.

sources.NUM_CORES, NUM_WARPS, NUM_THREADS, ISSUE: 108 SMs, 64 resident warps/SM, 4 schedulers x 32 lanes (NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU Architecture whitepaper, Table 3)
sources.FDIV_PE_RATIO, FSQRT_PE_RATIO, FCVT_PE_R: 16 results per clock per SM, 4 per processing block: FP32 reciprocal and reciprocal square root, on which division and square root are built, and all type conversions not to or from 8/16-bit integers (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput, compute capability 8.0); 16 FPU lanes / 4
sources.DCACHE_NUM_BANKS: 128 B per clock of L1 data per SM (A100 whitepaper): 4 banks of the 32 B dcache word. The default (one bank per LSU request channel) gives 8, twice the part
sources.DCACHE_SIZE: 192 KB combined L1/shared per SM (whitepaper): 6 ways over power-of-two sets
sources.L2_SIZE, L2_NUM_WAYS, L2_NUM_BANKS: 40 MB L2 in 80 slices (whitepaper): 20 ways over power-of-two sets; 64 banks of 64 B (4 KB/clk), the power of two nearest the 80 slices' 5 KB/clk
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_TYPE, PLATFORM_MEMORY_NU: 5 HBM2 stacks x 8 128-bit channels = 40 channels at 2430 MT/s, modelled as 32 channels at 3038 MT/s for a power-of-two interleave: 32 x 16 B x 3038 MT/s = 1555 GB/s, the card's bandwidth; the array timing is in nanoseconds, so latency is unchanged
sources.FETCH_WIDTH: 4 SM processing blocks, each with its own warp scheduler, dispatch unit and L0 instruction cache (NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU Architecture whitepaper)
sources.CP_LLC_CLIENT: Host copies reach device memory through the L2 like every other client, so uploaded data is L2-resident at launch
sources.LMEM_NUM_BANKS: 128 B per clock per SM: 32 banks of 4 B on the part (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, shared memory). Vortex banks are XLEN wide (8 B), so 16 banks carry the same bytes per clock; lanes reading one 8 B word share its bank access, so a stride-1 FP32 warp read is conflict-free as on the part
sources.VM_ENABLE, EXT_A_ENABLE, EXT_ZACAS_ENABL: Every NVIDIA GPU since Pascal has a demand-paged MMU (unified memory), global and shared-memory atomics with a native compare-and-swap (atomicCAS), FP16 storage and conversion, and per-partition special-function units for the transcendentals (MUFU)
sources.EXT_TCU_ENABLE, TCU_*, EXT_DXA_ENABLE, E: Third-generation tensor cores: FP16/BF16, TF32, INT8 and INT4, with 2:4 structured sparsity (A100 whitepaper). A100 has cp.async but no TMA, so no DXA
sources.xlen: 64-bit machine: 64-bit pointers and FP64 (the D extension follows XLEN=64), with a 48-bit device address space against NVIDIA's 49-bit virtual addresses; configure --profile picks a build64 tree and a build32 tree rejects the profile
sources.NUM_BARRIERS: 16 named CTA barriers (bar.sync 0-15, PTX ISA) on every NVIDIA GPU
sources.EXT_RASTER_ENABLE, EXT_OM_ENABLE: Off: the datacenter part is built for compute (no display outputs; the raster and ROP hardware is reduced or absent), so the profile models its compute machine
sources.NUM_MUFU_LANES: 16 special-function results per clock per SM (4 SFUs in each of the 4 processing blocks) for the reciprocal, reciprocal square root, log2, exp2, sine and cosine (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput, compute capability 8.0)
sources.NUM_ALU_LANES, NUM_FPU_LANES, NUM_LSU_LA: GA100 SM (A100 whitepaper, Figure 7): 4 processing blocks, each with 16 FP32, 16 INT32, 8 FP64 cores, 8 LD/ST units, 1 SFU and 1 tensor core. One Vortex ALU/FPU/LSU block per processing block (ISSUE_WIDTH=4) with the part's INT32, FP32 and LD/ST lanes; a 32-thread warp instruction issues over NUM_THREADS/lanes cycles, as on the part. The TCU stays full-warp (NUM_TCU_LANES == NUM_THREADS). FP64 is not modelled separately: with XLEN=64 each FPU lane also executes FP64, so the profile has 64 FP64 lanes per SM against the part's 32
sources.LMEM_SIZE, LMEM_LOG_SIZE, DCACHE_SIZE: 164 KB maximum shared memory per SM (CUDA Programming Guide, compute capability 8.0) in a 256 KB window. DCACHE_SIZE is the whole 192 KB L1/shared pool: the driver gives a kernel the L1 its shared-memory use leaves
sources.reference: fp32_lanes is the vendor FP32 core count (FP32 FMA lanes per chip, clock-free); dram_bandwidth_gbs the vendor peak. Checked by ci/profile_check.py. Latencies: Abdelkhalik et al., Demystifying the Nvidia Ampere Architecture through Microbenchmarking and Instruction-level Analysis (HPEC 2022), Table IV: L1 33, L2 200, global memory 290 cycles
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_QUEUE_SIZE: Per-channel request queue of GPGPU-Sim's SM80_A100 configuration (accel-sim gpu-simulator/configs/tested-cfgs/SM80_A100/gpgpusim.config)
sources.L2_LINK_LATENCY: 61 core cycles each way between an SM and the L2, the SM-to-L2 network, which the L2 bank pipeline (L2_LATENCY) does not model: calibrated with ci/profile_check.py so the SimX pointer chase gives the 200-cycle L2 hit latency in 'reference'
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_LATENCY: 11 core cycles of PHY/NoC latency beyond the L2 link, calibrated with ci/profile_check.py so the SimX cold pointer chase gives the 290-cycle global memory latency in 'reference' (GPGPU-Sim's SM80_A100 has a fixed latency of 190 and no link)
sources.L2_MSHR_SIZE: 32 per bank: Little's law on the L2-miss round trip ci/profile_check.py measures (DRAM 290 - L2 hit 200 = 90 cycles) x 1103 B/cycle (1555 GB/s / 1410 MHz) / (64 banks x 64 B) = 24.2, rounded up to a power of two. The derived default counts only PLATFORM_MEMORY_LATENCY, which the link latency now mostly replaces
